$comment: Machine-checkable claims made by the brand guides.
The guides make factual assertions about Lrnon — how many modules are live,
whether certification exists, whether the assistant is switched on. Those
assertions go stale the moment the product moves, and a brand guide that is
quietly wrong is worse than none: it gets pasted into a funding application.
This is the same problem the curriculum already solved. A tool description
older than 120 days fails the build (CUR-7); a vendor doc that changes is
reported by check-sources.mjs. Brand claims get the same treatment rather
Each entry names an `expect` value and the `probe` that measures reality.
scripts/check-brand-claims.mjs runs every probe and fails when one drifts,
naming the guide and the line to change. Update the guide AND this file
together — that is the point of the pairing.
reviewEveryDays sets the staleness rule for the guides themselves, the way
lastVerified does for a registry card.

claims.guideText: "Fourteen Explorer modules" — appears in the public statement and the funder guide.
claims.onDrift: Change the module count everywhere it appears. The funder guide compares it against Google AI Essentials' five, so that contrast moves too.

claims.guideText: Part B: "The Practitioner track is complete; Builder is not."
claims.onDrift: Update Part B. The Practitioner track is now complete, so the word incomplete applies to Builder only.

claims.guideText: Part B implies the Builder track has nothing published yet.
claims.onDrift: Part B must stop implying Builder is empty.

claims.guideText: "Certification is now built — schema, assessment, published rubric and verification page — but switched off."
claims.onDrift: The certification code has been removed or renamed. Both guides describe machinery that no longer exists; either restore it or take the description down.

claims.guideText: "No learner can obtain one yet." Part B: never imply a certificate is obtainable; do not demo an issued one.
claims.onDrift: Certification is now issuing. Both guides must stop saying no learner can obtain one, and Part B's do-not-demo instruction should go. Before changing a word, check the two human gates actually closed — two reviewers agreed on twenty samples, guardian path tested with real families — rather than someone having flipped the seed row.

claims.guideText: Part B: "The question-answering part of Sky is enabled for STAFF ONLY, as of 4 September 2026. Not for learners, not for the public." The study-buddy companion is separate and is on every page (see sky-companion-everywhere).
claims.onDrift: The deployed ceiling moved. If it went to 'slice' or 'everyone', Part B's 'no learner can reach it' is now false and must change the same day — and before changing a word, check the four gates actually closed on measured data rather than someone editing the GATES array in AdminSky.tsx. If it went back to 'off', say so plainly rather than leaving a claim that it is running.

claims.guideText: "Sky, a friendly study buddy, is on every page." It is the companion only: it answers nothing, awards nothing and sends nothing.
claims.onDrift: Base.astro no longer renders the Sky companion on every page, or renders it conditionally. Guides 02, 03 and 04 say it is on every page; either restore it or take the claim down.

claims.guideText: "Lrnon is open to donations, grants and advertising under published rules." Giving is open on /support (FUNDING_MODE = published).
claims.onDrift: FUNDING_MODE changed. If it went back to 'partial' or 'hidden', the guides must stop saying giving is open. Nothing has been raised, so say nothing more than the page does.

claims.guideText: "No advertisement is shown or approved." Advertising is permitted under the rules in funding-policy.js and none is shown (AD_MODE = off).
claims.onDrift: AD_MODE is no longer 'off'. Before changing a word: check ads.js has a real approved entry, that /privacy and /safeguarding describe what is shown, and that the first ledger row is published. Then update guides 03 and 04, which say none is shown.
ads.js now contains an entry. If it is real, the guides must say how many and who paid, and the ledger must show it.

claims.guideText: "Community features stay closed until a named safeguarding owner and deputy exist."
claims.onDrift: Rooms are open. Every guide claiming they are closed is now wrong, and the safeguarding claims need re-checking against what actually shipped.

claims.guideText: "Nobody pays to be in a lesson." Until 15 October 2026 this was "No sponsorship, ever" and covered all money; it now covers placement, ranking and inclusion only, because donations, grants and advertising are open. The load-bearing claim in all four guides.
claims.onDrift: Something in the codebase now references a sponsor, affiliate or paid placement. If that is real, every guide is wrong and the claim comes down the same day. Advertising under the published rules is not this: it is a labelled advertisement in ads.js, never placement in a lesson.

claims.guideText: "A tool description older than 120 days fails the build."
claims.onDrift: The threshold in validate-content.mjs changed. Update the number in the guides, or restore the threshold.
